question: May a Claw package register arbitrary host stdio commands in the global MCP registry, or must Claw MCP resources be brokered and scoped per agent or install?
rationale: The branch changes who may create host-executable MCP configuration and whether that resource is global; tests cannot determine the intended trust, authorization, and isolation model.

options.title: Broker and scope MCP resources
options.body: Require an allowlisted or host-approved command path, sanitize the child environment, namespace resources per agent or install, and make sharing an explicit host-authorized action.

options.title: Declare Claws host-trusted
options.body: Treat installing a Claw as equivalent to installing trusted host code and document that its MCP commands and global names receive operator-level authority.

options.title: Defer this lifecycle stage
options.body: Pause MCP ownership until the RFC and core MCP registry provide a stable scoped-resource and authorization contract.

recommendation.title: Broker and scope MCP resources
recommendation.body: Require an allowlisted or host-approved command path, sanitize the child environment, namespace resources per agent or install, and make sharing an explicit host-authorized action.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen is the assigned reviewer and has already reviewed the ownership, reconciliation, and persistent-state boundaries changed by this stack.
